pl-l4d2c4-d1e115.summary: Asks what John's baptism was useful for, and answers that it prepared people, through the practice of baptizing, for Christ's baptism.
claims: John's baptism prepared people for Christ's.

pl-l4d2c4-d1e121.summary: Asks why it is called John's baptism, as in 'the baptism of John, whence was it?': because there was only John's visible operation of washing outwardly, not God's invisible grace working inwardly. Yet John's action was from God, and that baptism was from God, not man; it was called man's because nothing was done there that man did not do.
claims: John's baptism is called his because it involved only outward human washing.

pl-l4d2c4.summary: Asks what use John's baptism had: it prepared people, by the practice of baptizing, for Christ's baptism. It is called John's baptism because only John's visible outward washing was there, not God's invisible inward grace; yet John's action and baptism were from God, called human because nothing happened there that man did not do.
claims: John's baptism prepared people for Christ's.
It is called John's because only an outward human action occurred in it.
John's baptism was nonetheless from God.
